sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 40957 of 2024

Applicant :- Praveen Verma And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Anand Kumar Srivastava,Siddharth Srivastava

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J.
The matter has been taken up through video conferencing.

Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants with the prayer to release them on bail during the trial in Case Crime No. 381 of 2024, under sections 34, 419, 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC and Section 66C, 66D of the I.T. Act P.S.- Naini, District-Prayagraj.
Contention of learned counsel for the applicants is that the applicants are innocent and have falsely been implicated in the instant matter due to ulterior motive.
He submits that certain articles are said to be recovered by the investigating officer, but he has failed to connect the applicants with the offence.

He further added that the recovery has been done at an open place, but there is no Praveen Verma And Another vs State Of U.P. on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110363627/
1 independent eye witness of either incident or recovery.

sentences.text: He further submits that the applicants have no previous criminal antecedents as is mentioned in paragraph no. 33 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application and they are languishing in jail since 10.6.2024 and they have undertaken that in case, they are granted bail, they will not misuse the liberty of the same and would cooperate in the trial proceedings.

Per contra, learned AGA appearing for the State has opposed the contentions aforesaid and submits that the applicants have been arrested while committing offence and certain articles have been recovered from their possession as such, they are not entitled for any relief.
Having heard learned counsels for the parties and after perusal of material placed on record, it transpires that prima facie, no such articles are said to be recovered from the possession of the applicants and recovery has been done at an open place, but there is no independent eye witness of either incident or recovery so as to connect them in the instant matter; the applicants have no previous criminal antecedents as is mentioned in paragraph no. 33 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application and they are languishing in jail since 10.6.2024 and they have undertaken that in case, they are granted bail, they will not misuse the liberty of the same and would cooperate in the trial proceedings.
Considering the submissions of learned counsels for the parties, nature of accusation and severity of punishment in case of conviction, nature of supporting evidence, prima facie satisfaction of the Court in support of the charge, reformative theory of punishment and considering larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and, without expressing any view on the merits of the case,
I find it to be a fit case of bail.
Let the applicants- Praveen Verma and Ghanshyam Verma involved in the aforementioned crime be released on bail, on their furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned, with the following conditions:-
(1) The applicants shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/
pressurizing the witnesses, or otherwise during the investigation or trial;
(2) The applicants shall file an undertaking to the effect that they shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
They shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through their counsel.

In case of their absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against them under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code;
(3) The applicants shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.; and (4) In case, the applicants misuse the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure their presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicants fail to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation

, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against them, in Praveen Verma And Another vs State Of U.P. on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110363627/
2 accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by the court concerned and in case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicants to prison.
It is clarified that the observations made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of this bail application and must not be construed to have any reflection on the merits of the case.
